The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full application with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. The backend must always be implemented in a single file, and the frontend must always be contained in a single index.html file, including all subpages.

Based on the technical architecture document, here is the complete implementation prompt: Autonomous AI Agent Development Platform Complete Implementation Specification Build a complete autonomous AIdriven software development platform with multiagent orchestration, browserbased testing, extended reasoning capabilities, and snapshotbased version control. The system must be productionready with all files complete and unabridged. Core Architecture Requirements 1. MultiAgent Orchestration System Implement a hierarchical multiagent architecture with: Main Agent Controller: Central orchestration component that processes user requests, generates code, coordinates subagents, performs highlevel task planning, and decomposes complex tasks into discrete subtasks. Testing Subagent: Specialized agent exclusively for testing operations. Receives highlevel action plans from the main agent, executes autonomous testing cycles, communicates via contextpassing mechanisms to minimize overhead, and operates independently once spawned. Code Generation Subagent: Ultrafast code synthesis using Cerebras GLM 4.7 model, capable of generating production code at 1000+ tokens per second, supporting multiple programming languages, and generating complete implementations with tests. 2. Autonomous Testing System Three Core Components BrowserBased Testing Engine: Integrate real browser automation (Playwright) to test applications. Display browser preview within agent panel showing agent cursor interactions. Test buttons, forms, APIs, and data sources. Capture screenshots and DOM states at each test step. Execute user flows endtoend. DOM Representation and Instrumentation: Provide strippeddown DOM representation enhanced with ARIA labels and test attributes. Automatically inject test attributes (data-testid) into generated code for interactive elements (form fields, buttons, links). Parse accessibility tree for semantic element identification. Utility Functions and Logging: Inject utility functions into execution context including readonly database query capabilities on development databases. Capture and log all new clientside and serverside logs since last execution. Implement printstyle debugging with automatic log correlation. Provide stack trace analysis and error contextualization. 3. Extended Thinking and Dynamic Intelligence Implement three intelligence modes: Extended Thinking Mode: Instructs agent to slow down and think deeply before acting. Shows stepbystep reasoning process before final output. Particularly useful for openended requests, complex problems, agents stuck in loops, and difficult debugging scenarios. Implement 3 depth levels (shallow, medium, deep) with progressively more reasoning tokens. High Power Model Mode: Switch to more capable AI model (Claude Opus 4.5) for increased accuracy. Use for application performance optimization, significant UI redesigns, complex database schema changes, intricate thirdparty API integrations, and architectural refactoring. Web Search Capability: Enable intelligent web searches to fill knowledge gaps. Query external documentation, search for library examples, fetch API specifications, and retrieve current best practices. 4. SelfTesting Loop and Execution Cycle Execution → Detection → Fix → Rerun Loop: After code generation, execute the code in sandbox. Detect errors through exception handling, log analysis, and test failures. Automatically generate fixes based on error analysis. Rerun code until tests pass or maximum iterations reached (default: 5 attempts). Snapshot Engine for Rollback: Implement copyonwrite snapshot system using: 16 MiB blocklevel chunking of virtual disks Immutable chunks stored in cloud storage (GCS/S3) Manifest files containing chunk pointers for each version Instant filesystem forking via manifest copying (O(1) time complexity) Versioned databases with pointintime recovery Isolated sandboxes for parallel agent execution Logarithmicallyspaced snapshot retention (Evan Wallace's algorithm) Cost Optimization: Target 3x speed improvement and 10x cost reduction compared to computeruse models. Median cost per testing session should be ~$0.20. 5. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration MCP Server Implementation: Support three MCP primitives: Resources: Expose code artifacts, documentation, and cached data Prompts: Provide reusable prompt templates for common tasks Tools: Expose agent capabilities (code generation, testing, reasoning) as callable tools Security Scanning: Route all MCP traffic through security scanner. Evaluate tool definitions for malicious instructions. Detect tool poisoning, shadowing attacks, and rug pulls. Block suspicious tools before execution. Authentication Methods: OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) with automatic client registration Custom headers (API keys, bearer tokens) Certificatebased authentication for enterprise deployments 6. Infrastructure Architecture Container Orchestration Layer: Singleregion cluster constraint to reduce latency Uniform cluster sizing with consistent hashing for workload distribution Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/Pulumi) for cluster provisioning Support for singletenant clusters for enterprise isolation Autoscaling based on agent workload Filesystem Architecture (Margarinestyle): Smart caching layer moving 16 MiB blocks between cloud storage, local SSD, and memory Network Block Device (NBD) architecture for virtual disks Blocklevel caching with LRU/LFU eviction policies Dynamic cache management based on access patterns Backup service (Backer) for automated cloud storage backups via pub/sub notifications Package Management (Nix Integration): Hashbased package store (/nix/store/--) Dependency isolation solving dependency hell Configuration via replit.nix files specifying package dependencies Automatic builds with Nixpacks for multiple language ecosystems Reproducible environments across deployments Database Layer (PostgreSQL): Serverless PostgreSQL (Neoncompatible) Ondemand scaling based on query load Alembic migration support with upgrade/downgrade functions Strict separation: production databases (readonly from agent), development databases (full access) Snapshotbased database forking for testing Technology Stack Implementation 1. Modal.com for Serverless GPU Compute Use Modal as primary compute platform with these specifications: B200 GPU Configuration: NVIDIA B200 Blackwell architecture 180 GB GPU RAM 8 TB/s memory bandwidth Native FP4 tensor operations (9 PFLOPS) FP8 tensor operations (5 PFLOPS) 16,896 CUDA cores 528 Tensor cores NVLink 5 (1,800 GB/s interconnect) Function Definitions: Create Modal functions with: GPU selection: gpu="B200" Memory allocation: memory=32768 (32 GB RAM minimum) Timeout: timeout=12000 (200 minutes for autonomous operation) Container idle timeout: container_idle_timeout=300 Volume mounts for persistent workspace storage Secret management for API keys (AWS, Cerebras, Dragonfly) Cost Model: B200 at $6.25/hour, payperuse billing, automatic scaletozero when idle. 2. AWS Bedrock Claude Opus 4.5 for Reasoning Reasoning Engine Configuration: Model ID: anthropic.claude-opus-4-5 Anthropic version: bedrock-2023-05-31 Temperature: 0.7 for balanced creativity/accuracy Max tokens: 40968192 depending on task complexity System prompts for extended thinking, code review, architecture design Bedrock Agents and AgentCore: Multistep task execution Dynamic tool invocation Context retention across multiturn interactions Integration with AWS IAM for access control VPC isolation for network security Guardrails for content filtering and policy enforcement CrossPlatform Availability: Support deployment on Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Foundry for multicloud strategies. 3. Dragonfly Cloud for HighPerformance Caching Dragonfly Specifications: 25x throughput vs Redis 30% better memory efficiency 80% cost reduction Multithreaded architecture (vs Redis singlethreaded) Dashtable data structure for compact storage Forkless snapshotting (no memory spikes) 12x faster snapshots (1,260 MB/s) LRFU eviction policy (zero overhead) Full Redis API compatibility Cache Strategy: Agent session states with 1hour TTL Code context and dependency graphs Testing results with code hash as key Reasoning outputs for reuse Performance metrics and analytics 4.
